case_title: Govindaraju @ Govinda v. State by Sriramapuram P.S.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: an earlier police complaint of a fight between the accused and the deceased, as recounted by the victim's brother; the Court used this to doubt the accused's involvement
evidence_type: Eyewitness (a police officer, PW-1, as sole eyewitness); recovery evidence (seizure and disclosure-based); medical evidence (post-mortem); forensic (FSL) report
confession: None. Recoveries linked to disclosure statements were found defective and not relied upon against the accused.
aggravating_circumstances: Ten stab injuries to the chest recorded in the post-mortem; the Court did not weigh these as aggravating for sentencing
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of IPC s.302 read with s.34
high_court_outcome: Leave to appeal granted against the accused; acquittal set aside; convicted under IPC s.302 and sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs.10,000
neutral_facts: On 7 December 1998, at about 10.45 p.m., a police sub-inspector returning from duty on his motorcycle reportedly saw three men chasing another man near a bar. The pursued man fell to the road, and the chasers stabbed him repeatedly on the chest with a knife. The officer, about 30 yards away, said one of the attackers told another to run because police were coming, and the group fled into a nearby conservancy area. The officer chased them but could not catch them. He returned, found the injured man, and with the help of a constable took him to hospital, where he was declared dead. An identity card in the victim's pockets identified him. The officer then lodged a written complaint at the police station, on which the first information report was registered. The investigating officer recorded witness statements and recovered knives and blood-soaked earth, and the items were sent to the forensic laboratory. The post-mortem recorded ten stab injuries to the chest, with death attributed to shock and haemorrhage. Several eyewitnesses later did not support the officer's account. The recovery memos lacked the accused's signatures on the disclosure statements, and the recovery witnesses did not support the recoveries. One knife recovered at another accused's instance was blood-stained, but it was not established whether the blood was human or of the victim's blood group. The head constable, the constable and the doctor were not examined, and no forensic expert testified.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from shock and haemorrhage due to ten stab injuries, chiefly to the chest
key_evidence_accepted: Post-mortem report establishing knife injuries to the chest. The Court found the sole eyewitness's account unreliable and did not accept the recovery evidence against the accused.
witness_credibility: The sole eyewitness, a police officer (PW-1), was held not reliable: he was about 30 yards away on a motorcycle, did not name the accused in the FIR or to the investigating officer, and was not corroborated. Other eyewitnesses (PW-2, PW-7, PW-9, PW-10) turned hostile. The investigating officer (PW-11) was found to have left material witnesses unexamined.
post_offence_conduct: Alleged: after the attack the assailants fled into a conservancy area when police approached (prosecution version of PW-1; not established by the Court)
bail_history: Bail and surety bonds existed; the Supreme Court ordered the accused set at liberty and the bonds discharged. Earlier bail details not stated.
trial_duration: offence: 7 December 1998; trial judgment: 9 March 2000; High Court: 29 November 2006; Supreme Court: 15 March 2012
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Rajesh Mahale, Krutin R. Joshi. State (respondents): Anitha Shenoy, Hetu Arora
investigation_status: FIR registered on the police officer's complaint; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; trial completed in the Sessions court
procedural_irregularity: Doctor, head constable, constable and FSL expert not examined; recovery memos lacked accused's signatures on disclosure statements; blood group of the stained knife not proved
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted (9 March 2000). High Court: leave granted against the accused, conviction under s.302 and life imprisonment (29 November 2006). Supreme Court: appeal allowed, accused acquitted.
prosecution_argument: The State contended the case was not one of false implication; PW-1 was the eyewitness; weapons were recovered from the appellant's house; panchas admitted their signatures; the collective documentary and ocular evidence proved guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
defence_argument: All witnesses turned hostile; the sole police eyewitness was interested and the accused was falsely implicated; no independent witnesses; recovery not proved under s.27 Evidence Act; no seizure witness; ocular evidence not supported by medical or scientific evidence; the accused's role was lesser than that of the co-accused whose acquittal had become final.
legal_principle_applied: In an appeal against acquittal, presumption of innocence is reinforced; interference only where the trial judgment is perverse, with a clear distinction between perversity and merely another possible view. Police testimony must be reliable, trustworthy and corroborated; hostile witnesses' supportive parts may be used; adverse inference may be drawn for withholding material witnesses.
precedent_relied_upon: Girja Prasad v. State of MP (2007) 7 SCC 625; State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram (2012) 1 SCC 602; C. Antony v. K.G. Raghavan Nair (2003) 1 SCC 1; Bhim Singh Rup Singh v. State of Maharashtra (1974) 3 SCC 762; Lallu Manjhi v. State of Jharkhand (2003) 2 SCC 401; Joseph v. State of Kerala (2003) 1 SCC 465; Tika Ram v. State of MP (2007) 15 SCC 760; Jhapsa Kabari v. State of Bihar (2001) 10 SCC 94; Tahir v. State (Delhi) (1996) 3 SCC 338; Takhaji Hiraji v. Thakore Kubersing Chamansing (2001) 6 SCC 145; Yakub Ismailbhai Patel v. State of Gujarat (2004) 12 SCC 229; State Govt. of NCT of Delhi v. Sunil (2001) 1 SCC 652
other_sentence_order: Accused to be set at liberty forthwith; bail and surety bonds discharged
